description: What the data in a genomic annotation file represents, split into an algorithmic interpretation (output_type, drawing on the DataType vocabulary) and a biological interpretation (feature_type, drawing on the FeatureType vocabulary). Corresponds to FGA-WG issue #2.

element_type.description: The Sequence Ontology class(es) that the individual rows/records of this track instantiate. One value = a homogeneous set; several values = a mixed set (rows may be instances of any listed class); absent = the rows are not SO-typeable features (signal values, matrices, models, edges). This is a CONTENT facet — it answers *what the rows are* — so it lives on TrackInterpretation, not TrackProvenance (design principle #4). It is the slot form of the `onga:has_element_type` relation: an ONGA term denotes a SET of elements, an SO class denotes the element type, and ONGA never asserts equivalence between them (design principle #7).

feature_type.description: The biological interpretation: the biological entity or concept the data represents (e.g. TF binding site, enhancer, CpG island). Draws on the FeatureType vocabulary.

haplotype_resolution.description: The haplotype resolution the file represents: whether content is resolved to individual alleles (allele_specific), partitioned per parental haplotype (haplotype_specific), or phase-resolved without per-haplotype splitting (phased). A content facet factored out of compound DataType/FeatureType terms (e.g. "haplotype-specific contact matrix", "phased variant calls"). Absent means haplotype-collapsed / not phase-resolved.

output_type.description: The algorithmic interpretation: the computational process or output the file represents (e.g. peaks, signal, alignment, count matrix). Draws on the DataType vocabulary.

strand.description: The strand orientation the file represents. Factored out of compound DataType terms (e.g. "minus strand signal"). Absent means unstranded/unspecified.

title: TrackInterpretation
